'''Lawrence David (Larry) Brown''' (16 December 1940 – 21 February 2018)<ref name="statsci_2005">{{cite journal|title=A Conversation with Larry Brown|last=DasGupta|first=Anirban|journal=[[Statistical Science]]|volume=20|issue=2|pages=193–203|year=2019|doi=10.1214/088342304000000288 |s2cid=123440029 |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.imsc/1288099003|chapter=Biography of Lawrence D. Brown|editor1-first=James O. |editor1-last=Berger| editor1-link=James Berger (statistician)|editor2-first=T. Tony |editor2-last=Cai| editor2-link=T. Tony Cai| editor3-first=Iain M. |editor3-last=Johnstone |title=Borrowing Strength: Theory Powering Applications – A Festschrift for Lawrence D. Brown |location=Beachwood, Ohio, USA|publisher=[[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] |year=2010|volume=6 | pages=ix-x}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Lawrence Brown|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/lawrence-d-brown-wfbkt9/|access-date=2020-06-08|website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref> was Miers Busch Professor and Professor of [[Statistics]] at the [[Wharton School]] of the [[University of Pennsylvania]] in [[Philadelphia]], Pennsylvania. He is known for his groundbreaking work in a broad range of fields including [[decision theory]], [[Markov_chain#Properties|recurrence]] and [[partial differential equation]]s, nonparametric function estimation, minimax and adaptation theory, and the analysis of [[US Census|census]] data and [[Call centre|call-center]] data.<ref name=":3" />

== Career ==
Brown was educated at the [[California Institute of Technology]] and [[Cornell University]], where he earned his Ph.D. in 1964.  He earned numerous honors, including election to the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]], and published widely, beginning with his Ph.D. research, which made major advances in [[Admissible decision rule|admissibility]].<ref name="statsci_2005"/> He was president of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] in 1992–93. He was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2013.<ref name=":1">[http://amacad.org/news/classlist2013.pdf Newly elected members] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130501223006/http://www.amacad.org/news/classlist2013.pdf|date=2013-05-01}}, [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], April 2013, retrieved 2013-04-24.</ref>

After having been assistant professor at [[University of California at Berkeley]], associate professor at [[Cornell University]]{{snd}}with the latter move entailing a change from a statistics to a mathematics department, allowing him to avoid being drafted for the [[Vietnam War]]<ref name="statsci_2005"/>{{snd}}and professor at [[Cornell University]] and [[Rutgers University]], he was invited to join the Department of Statistics at the [[Wharton School]] of the [[University of Pennsylvania]].

== Personal life ==
Brown was born in Los Angeles to parents [[Louis M. Brown]] and Hermione Brown. He was married to [[Linda Zhao]], a fellow statistician at the Wharton School.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Institute of Mathematical Statistics {{!}} Obituary: Lawrence Brown, 1940–2018|url=https://imstat.org/2018/05/15/obituary-lawrence-brown-1940-2018/|access-date=2020-06-16}}</ref>

* Member, [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref name=":1" />
* Member, [[National Academy of Sciences]]<ref name=":0" />
* Fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]] (A.S.A)<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Lawrence D. Brown|url=http://www-stat.wharton.upenn.edu/~lbrown/|access-date=2020-06-08|website=www-stat.wharton.upenn.edu}}</ref>
* Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] (I.M.S.)<ref name=":2" />
* Wald Lecturer, [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]], August 1985;<ref>{{Cite web|title=Institute of Mathematical Statistics {{!}} Honored Special Lecturers Recipient List|url=https://imstat.org/ims-special-lectures/honored-special-lecturers-recipient-list/|access-date=2020-06-08|language=en|archive-date=2021-11-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211123172824/https://imstat.org/ims-special-lectures/honored-special-lecturers-recipient-list/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
*Lady Davis Professorship, [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem|Hebrew University]], 1988<ref name=":2" />
*Doctor of Science (Honorary), [[Purdue University]], 1993<ref>{{Cite web|last=Purdue University|date=|title=Honorary Doctorate Degrees, 1888-Current|url=https://www.purdue.edu/bot/honorary-doctorates/alphabetical.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200608183242/https://www.purdue.edu/bot/honorary-doctorates/alphabetical.pdf|archive-date=2020-06-08|access-date=|website=|url-status=dead}}</ref>
*[[Wilks Memorial Award|Wilks Award of the American Statistical Association]], 2002<ref name=":2" />
* [[C. R. Rao#In his honour|C.R. and B. Rao Prize]], 2007<ref>{{Cite web|last=Penn State Eberly College of Science Department of Statistics|date=|title=C. R. Rao and Bhargavi Prize|url=https://science.psu.edu/stat/rao-prize|access-date=|website=}}</ref>
* The Provost's Award for Distinguished Ph.D. Teaching and Mentoring, [[University of Pennsylvania]], 2011<ref>{{Cite web|title=Provost's Awards • University Archives and Records Center|url=https://archives.upenn.edu/exhibits/penn-people/notables/awards/provost|access-date=2020-06-08|website=University Archives and Records Center|language=en-US}}</ref>
